sentences.text: Florida’s waters are full of tugs: fuel barges on the Intracoastal, dredge pipe in the inlets, big ocean tows off the coast.
A tow is the most dangerous thing you can misread at night, because there may be hundreds of feet of cable between the tug and whatever she’s pulling.
Rule twenty-four tells you how to spot one.
A vessel towing astern shows a yellow towing light directly above her white sternlight.
If you’re coming up behind those two lights, something is trailing behind her, between you and the tug.
A power-driven vessel towing astern shows two masthead lights in a vertical line, plus sidelights.
Two white lights stacked means a tow of two hundred meters or less.
And when the tow is longer than two hundred meters, she shows three masthead lights in a vertical line.
From the stern of the towing vessel to the after end of the tow.
By day, a tow over two hundred meters is marked with a diamond shape, on both the towing vessel and the tow.
And a tug of fifty meters or more still carries her other masthead light as well.
